best-broadway-shows.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows in March 2026

As Broadway enters the spring season of 2026, the Great White Way offers an impressive mix of long-running classics, acclaimed revivals, and breakout hits. This month's top-rated productions average an 84/100 critic score, reflecting a particularly strong theatrical landscape where audiences can choose from groundbreaking new work alongside beloved staples.

**Hamilton** continues its historic run at the top of the rankings, with critics still celebrating Lin-Manuel Miranda's hip-hop retelling of American history as a revolutionary achievement in musical theater. The show's fusion of contemporary music with founding-era politics remains as vital and relevant as ever, nearly a decade after its Broadway debut.

Among newer productions, **Maybe Happy Ending** stands out as a surprising critical darling. This unconventional robot love story earns praise for its emotional depth and originality, proving that Broadway still has room for intimate, inventive storytelling. Meanwhile, **Oh, Mary!** has become the comedy sensation of the season, with Cole Escola's absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln drawing raves for its fearless irreverence.

The month's lineup also showcases Broadway's enduring classics—**The Lion King** and **Chicago** demonstrate the staying power of innovative staging and sharp satire, while **The Book of Mormon** continues to provoke and entertain. The timely revival of **Ragtime** brings renewed relevance to its exploration of race and justice in America, anchored by Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance.

Whether you're drawn to spectacle, comedy, drama, or innovative storytelling, March 2026 presents an opportunity to experience Broadway at a creative high point across multiple genres and styles.

best-broadway-musicals.intro:

Broadway enters spring 2026 with a remarkably strong lineup that balances enduring classics with fresh voices, achieving an impressive average critic score of 83 out of 100 across our top ten musicals.

**Hamilton** continues its reign as the highest-rated show on Broadway, with critics still marveling at Lin-Manuel Miranda's revolutionary hip-hop musical nearly eleven years after its premiere. The show's 90/100 score reflects its sustained artistic impact and relevance. Meanwhile, **Maybe Happy Ending** emerges as one of the season's most pleasant surprises—this charming robot love story earns an 85/100 rating as critics praise it as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years, proving that innovative storytelling still finds a home on the Great White Way.

The current landscape showcases Broadway's remarkable range: **Toni Collette** and **Ariana DeBose** lead the timely **Ragtime** revival to strong reviews, while perennial favorites like **The Lion King** and **Chicago** demonstrate why certain productions become institutions. Folk-opera **Hadestown** and irreverent satire **The Book of Mormon** represent the past decade's most successful new voices, while **Buena Vista Social Club** brings intoxicating Latin rhythms to the stage despite narrative shortcomings. The pop-infused **SIX** continues to draw crowds with its modern reimagining of Tudor history, and Jonathan Groff commands attention in the Bobby Darin bio-musical **Just in Time**.

This diverse collection of musicals—spanning hip-hop history lessons, robot romances, Greek mythology, and jukebox tributes—illustrates Broadway's current vitality and its ability to honor tradition while embracing innovation. Whether you're seeking groundbreaking artistry or polished entertainment, March 2026 offers compelling options across the spectrum.

best-broadway-plays.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway enters the spring season, the landscape of straight plays offers an intriguing mix of intimate character studies and spectacular technical achievements. This month's top-rated productions range from absurdist comedy to wizarding world drama, with an average critic score of 78 out of 100 across four featured shows.

Leading the pack is **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's irreverent reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed, alcohol-fueled narcissist. The absurdist farce earns the highest marks this month, with critics celebrating its riotous humor and bold comedic vision. Close behind, **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** continues to impress audiences with its jaw-dropping stagecraft and magical illusions, though reviewers note the narrative doesn't quite match the production's technical brilliance.

On the more intimate end of the spectrum, **Every Brilliant Thing** showcases Daniel Radcliffe in a warmly received solo performance that tackles depression and life's small joys through audience interaction. The production demonstrates that Broadway's appeal extends beyond spectacle to genuinely human storytelling.

Meanwhile, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** represents the growing trend of screen-to-stage adaptations, delivering impressive special effects and technical wizardry even as critics find its three-hour runtime and prequel storytelling somewhat overstuffed.

This month's selection reflects Broadway's current identity crisis and creative vitality—torn between intimate theatrical experiences and blockbuster spectacles designed to compete with streaming entertainment. Whether you're drawn to sharp-witted comedy, magical escapism, or heartfelt solo performances, March offers distinct options worth considering for your next theater outing.

best-broadway-shows-for-kids.intro:

Close behind, **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** scores 82/100 across 69 reviews, with critics consistently praising its spectacular stagecraft and magical illusions, even as they note narrative inconsistencies in the story itself.

The current landscape reflects Broadway's heavy reliance on established intellectual property, with Disney's **Aladdin** (71/100) joining The Lion King as a family draw, while **Wicked** (69/100) continues its remarkable long-term run despite mixed critical reception. Newer additions like the Shakespeare-inspired jukebox musical **& Juliet** (71/100) and **MJ The Musical** (69/100) demonstrate the industry's ongoing experimentation with familiar names and music catalogs to attract multi-generational audiences.

What stands out across these six productions is the emphasis on visual spectacle—whether through puppetry, magic effects, or choreography—as the primary vehicle for engaging younger theatergoers. Critics consistently rate technical achievements more highly than narrative elements, suggesting that Broadway's family offerings prioritize the "wow factor" over storytelling depth.

For families planning their Broadway experience this month, these scores and critical perspectives can help match shows to your children's ages, attention spans, and interests.

best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted. The season that began with such promise was abruptly cut short, making the handful of productions that premiered before the pandemic shutdown all the more significant in theater history.

Among the five shows from this truncated season still worth examining, **Les Misérables** leads the pack with its grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. Critics largely embrace this reimagined production, though purists remain divided on its darker interpretation of the beloved musical.

**A Soldier's Play** stands as perhaps the most critically significant arrival, bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer-winning drama to Broadway for the first time in a stellar revival. Nearly six years later, its examination of racial tensions within a segregated Army unit remains powerfully relevant, earning widespread critical acclaim across 29 reviews.

The season's other notable entries include **Grand Horizons**, a pleasant if familiar comedy elevated by performances from Jane Alexander, and **My Name is Lucy Barton**, which showcases Laura Linney's luminous solo work in this adaptation of Elizabeth Strout's novel, even as critics debate the material's theatrical merits.

Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves the most divisive, with its bold video design and visceral approach splitting critical opinion down the middle.

With an average critic score of 75/100, these five productions represent a strong if abbreviated season—a reminder of what was and what might have been. For theater enthusiasts exploring this pivotal moment in Broadway history, these shows offer essential viewing and context for understanding how the art form evolved through unprecedented disruption.

best-broadway-shows-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2021

As Broadway enters March 2026, the shows that reopened and debuted during the industry's historic 2021 return continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power. That watershed year—when theaters finally raised their curtains after an 18-month pandemic closure—produced an exceptionally strong slate of productions, with our featured shows averaging an impressive 81/100 critical score.

The year's offerings span an unusually wide artistic spectrum. Experimental works like **Dana H.**, featuring Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance to a real-life trauma narrative, and **Is This a Room**, which transforms a verbatim FBI transcript into gripping theater, push the boundaries of what Broadway can be. Meanwhile, **The Phantom of the Opera**—which began its record-breaking run decades earlier—proves that spectacle and melody still have their place alongside innovation.

Epic storytelling finds expression in **The Lehman Trilogy**, which traces 150 years of American capitalism through one family's rise and fall, while intimate character studies emerge in **Lackawanna Blues**, with Ruben Santiago-Hudson embodying dozens of figures from his childhood. The season also embraces bold reimaginings: **Company** gender-swaps Sondheim's protagonist to fresh effect, and **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** transforms the entire Playhouse Theatre into an immersive Weimar-era nightclub.

From Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's **Pass Over**, which served as Broadway's powerful reopening statement on Black American experience, to the pop-infused irreverence of **SIX** and Lynn Nottage's compassionate **Clyde's**, these productions capture a theater community emerging from crisis with renewed creative ambition. Whether you're drawn to experimental documentary theater or reimagined classics, this collection offers essential viewing for understanding Broadway's post-pandemic evolution.

best-broadway-shows-2022.intro:

As we reach March 2026, the remarkable class of 2022 Broadway productions continues to resonate with audiences and critics alike. That season proved to be a watershed moment for American theater, delivering an extraordinary concentration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works alongside inventive revivals that redefined classic material.

Leading the pack is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical that critics consistently describe as a near-perfect achievement, masterfully balancing laugh-out-loud comedy with genuine emotional depth. Close behind, **Into the Woods** stands as a triumphant tribute to Stephen Sondheim, with its stripped-down approach revealing new layers in the beloved score. **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's audacious meta-musical, continues to earn acclaim for its brazenly original voice and unflinching honesty.

The 2022 season's defining characteristic is its celebration of Pulitzer-winning dramatists. Alongside A Strange Loop's recent Pulitzer recognition, the season brought revivals and new productions of works by Suzan-Lori Parks (**Topdog/Underdog**), Paula Vogel (**How I Learned to Drive**), Stephen Adly Guirgis (**Between Riverside and Crazy**), and Martyna Majok (**Cost of Living**), each earning strong critical reception. Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt** adds gravitas as a haunting meditation on Jewish identity and loss.

The featured shows average an impressive 83 out of 100 from critics, reflecting a season that prioritized artistic ambition and diverse voices. From Jordan E. Cooper's provocative satire **Ain't No Mo'** to Mike Birbiglia's intimate storytelling in **The Old Man & The Pool**, these productions represent Broadway at its most vital and varied.

Whether you're seeking innovative musicals, powerful drama, or thought-provoking comedy, the 2022 season offers exceptional theater that continues to reward audiences nearly four years later.

best-broadway-shows-2023.intro:

The season's crown jewel remains **Merrily We Roll Along**, Maria Friedman's revelatory revival that finally unlocked the emotional core of Sondheim's famously troubled 1981 musical. Critics have embraced it as a genuine triumph, with an impressive 85/100 average across 31 reviews. Equally acclaimed is **Stranger Things: The First Shadow**, a West End transfer that demonstrates how intellectual property can be transformed into breathtaking, technically innovative theatre rather than mere fan service.

The year also delivered powerful dramatic work. **Appropriate**, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama starring Sarah Paulson, earned recognition as a modern American masterpiece, while **Purlie Victorious** brought Ossie Davis's 1961 satire back to Broadway with bracingly relevant results. Ben Platt and Micaela Diamond's performances in **Parade** reminded audiences why classic musicals deserve reconsideration for new generations.

Solo performances proved particularly strong, with Alex Edelman's **Just for Us** and Jodie Comer's **Prima Facie** both earning critical acclaim for their intimate, challenging material. Meanwhile, **Fat Ham**'s Pulitzer-winning reimagining of Hamlet and the infectious Cuban rhythms of **Buena Vista Social Club** added welcome diversity to the theatrical landscape.

With an average critic score of 82/100 across these productions, 2023's legacy shows continue to offer compelling reasons to experience Broadway at its most ambitious and accomplished.

The season also sees revivals and reimaginings of familiar titles. **Little Women the Musical** returns to Broadway with Louisa May Alcott's cherished story, though initial reception suggests the production struggles to distinguish itself in a crowded field of previous adaptations. Meanwhile, **The Little Mermaid the Musical** and **Gobstopper** round out the early offerings, both awaiting their critical debuts.

With an average critical score of 40 out of 100 across reviewed productions, the 2026 musical season reflects Broadway's ongoing challenge of balancing innovation with audience expectations. The wide variance in reception—from enthusiastic praise to lukewarm responses—underscores how even well-known properties require fresh creative vision to resonate with contemporary audiences.

As more productions open and accumulate reviews throughout the spring, theatergoers should monitor how these shows develop and which productions gain momentum with both critics and audiences.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating cross-section of theatrical ambition—from bold reimaginings of classics to long-awaited premieres cut short by the pandemic's arrival that spring.

Leading our selection is **Les Misérables**, which earns the highest critical marks with its grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This darker interpretation of the beloved musical demonstrates how classic material can be successfully reconsidered for contemporary audiences, though the approach doesn't win over every critic.

**A Soldier's Play** stands as perhaps the most significant artistic achievement from this period—Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally made its Broadway debut after nearly four decades, and critics largely agree the wait was worthwhile. The production's examination of race, power, and justice within a World War II-era Army base resonates with remarkable urgency, proving the play's themes remain painfully relevant.

The season also featured **West Side Story** in Ivo van Hove's polarizing reinvention, which strips away traditional choreography in favor of raw physicality and video design. It exemplifies the risk-taking that defined several 2020 productions, even if critics remain sharply divided on its success.

Rounding out the list are **Grand Horizons**, a well-acted if conventional comedy about late-life divorce, and **My Name is Lucy Barton**, which showcases Laura Linney's acclaimed solo performance in an intimate adaptation that critics find either deeply moving or dramatically inert.

With an average critical score of 75/100 across these five productions, the 2020 play season offered solid, if not spectacular, theatrical experiences—browse our detailed reviews below to find which productions align with your theatrical tastes.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that debuted in 2021 represent a watershed moment for American theater—the industry's triumphant return following an unprecedented shutdown. These productions arrived carrying both the weight of Broadway's darkest period and the electric energy of its resurrection, resulting in a season that critics found remarkably ambitious and artistically daring.

The standout among this group is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama that critics describe as mesmerizing and unforgettable, anchored by Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance to her mother's recorded testimony. Meanwhile, **The Lehman Trilogy** offers a vastly different theatrical experience—an epic three-act drama that critics praise as a theatrical triumph, featuring extraordinary ensemble performances and stunning direction that traces 163 years of American capitalism through one family's rise and fall.

The urgency of reopening Broadway also brought forth **Pass Over**, Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's powerful drama that critics hailed as a worthy first show back, blending Samuel Beckett and the Book of Exodus to examine Black American experience. Alongside these critical darlings, the season balanced experimental works like **Is This a Room**—a verbatim FBI transcript transformed into pulse-pounding theater—with crowd-pleasing revivals including a gender-swapped **Company** and the immersive **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club**.

With an average critic score of 81/100 across these ten productions, the class of 2021 demonstrates exceptional quality born from necessity and reinvention. Whether you're drawn to intimate solo performances, sweeping historical epics, or bold reimaginings of classics, these plays offer a compelling snapshot of Broadway at its most resilient.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable period of theatrical achievement, with an impressive collection of critically acclaimed productions that continue to resonate with audiences today.

The season's crown jewel is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical about a teenage girl with a rare aging condition that critics consistently describe as a near-perfect balance of comedy and heartbreak. Close behind is a stripped-down revival of **Into the Woods**, which served as a fitting tribute to Stephen Sondheim following his passing, with critics praising its stellar performances and fresh interpretation of the classic musical. **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical, rounds out the top tier with its brazenly original and brutally honest exploration of a Black queer artist's inner life.

What's particularly striking about this season is the prominence of Pulitzer Prize winners—both recent and classic. From Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog** to Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt**, the year showcased drama at its finest. The season also featured revivals of Paula Vogel's **How I Learned to Drive** and Stephen Adly Guirgis's **Between Riverside and Crazy**, alongside contemporary Pulitzer winner **Cost of Living** by Martyna Majok.

The ten featured productions average an impressive 83 out of 100 from critics, reflecting a season that balanced innovative new voices with reverent revivals of modern classics. Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting favorites, this collection represents some of the most accomplished theatrical work of the decade.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the Broadway plays that debuted in 2023 continue to demonstrate the enduring power of theatrical storytelling, with several productions maintaining strong critical reputations and cultural relevance nearly three years after their openings.

The year proved particularly significant for revivals that recontextualized classic works. Maria Friedman's production of **Merrily We Roll Along** stands as the highest-rated play from 2023, with critics celebrating how this staging finally unlocked the emotional resonance of Sondheim's previously troubled musical. The show's success represents one of Broadway's most satisfying redemption stories. Meanwhile, **Appropriate** earns acclaim as a searing family drama featuring Sarah Paulson in a blistering ensemble performance that critics describe as modern masterpiece material.

The 2023 season also showcased Broadway's commitment to diverse voices and urgent contemporary themes. The revival of **Purlie Victorious: A Non-Confederate Romp Through the Cotton Patch** brought Ossie Davis's 1961 satire back to Broadway with critics noting its surprising relevance six decades later, while **Parade** resonated with audiences for its timely exploration of prejudice and injustice. Solo performances proved particularly strong, with shows like **Just for Us** and **Prima Facie** demonstrating the continued vitality of one-person theatrical experiences.

With an average critical score of 82/100 across these ten productions, the 2023 Broadway play season reflects a year of artistic ambition and achievement. Whether you're drawn to reimagined classics, bold new voices, or powerhouse performances, these productions offer multiple entry points into contemporary theatre at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the shows that premiered in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This curated selection of ten productions—averaging an impressive 84/100 critical score—showcases the diversity and artistic ambition currently defining the American theater landscape.

Leading the field is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's 1970s rock drama that critics consistently describe as a theatrical marvel for its authentic exploration of the creative process. The production has accumulated 22 reviews praising its immersive depiction of a band at work, establishing it as one of the season's most significant dramatic achievements.

Musical theater proves equally vibrant with standout productions like **Maybe Happy Ending**, a robot love story that critics hail as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years, and the unexpected triumph of **Operation Mincemeat**, a grassroots sensation that earned its way from smaller venues to Broadway through sheer inventive energy. Meanwhile, **CATS: The Jellicle Ball** demonstrates how radical reimagining can breathe new life into established properties, infusing the Andrew Lloyd Webber classic with ballroom culture to critical acclaim.

Comedy finds its voice in **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln that has become a word-of-mouth sensation, while classic revivals like George C. Wolfe's **Gypsy** starring Audra McDonald and a lavish new **Oliver!** prove the enduring power of musical theater's golden age when executed with fresh perspective.

Whether you're drawn to innovative new voices or reimagined classics, this collection represents the breadth of theatrical excellence currently available on Broadway stages.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2025

As March 2026 unfolds, Broadway audiences continue to enjoy an impressive array of productions that debuted throughout 2025, with the season proving particularly strong for both bold new works and thoughtfully reimagined classics.

The year's theatrical offerings achieve an impressive average critic score of 84/100 across our top ten selections, reflecting a season marked by artistic ambition and consistent quality. Leading the pack is Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons**, which earns widespread acclaim for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work. Close behind, the 20th-anniversary production of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** reminds audiences why this quirky musical endures, with critics praising its airtight writing and perfect timing.

The season demonstrates remarkable range, from the theatrical marvel of **Paddington The Musical**—featuring a remarkably lifelike bear puppet that has enchanted critics—to Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English**, which offers a smart, sensitive exploration of language and identity. Musical theater shines particularly bright, with a timely **Ragtime** revival showcasing Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance, while **Dead Outlaw** brings darkly comic energy to the story of Elmer McCurdy's bizarre afterlife.

Branden Jacobs-Jenkins adds to his formidable body of work with **Purpose**, delivering another searing family drama, while Martyna Majok's **Liberation** presents an ambitious feminist memory play that critics find both timely and moving. Even productions with structural critiques, like the music-rich **Buena Vista Social Club**, offer undeniable theatrical pleasures.

Whether you're drawn to intimate character studies or spectacular musical experiences, this season's offerings provide compelling reasons to return to Broadway.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the season showcases an intimate approach to theatrical storytelling, with solo performances and deeply personal narratives taking center stage.

Leading the year's offerings is **Every Brilliant Thing**, which earns an impressive 81/100 from critics. Daniel Radcliffe commands the stage in this interactive solo show that tackles depression and mental health through an unexpectedly uplifting lens. The production invites audience participation as it chronicles one person's lifelong list of reasons to stay alive—from simple pleasures like ice cream to profound human connections. Critics consistently praise Radcliffe's warmth and accessibility in the role, noting how he creates genuine intimacy even in larger theater spaces. The show's format, which breaks down the fourth wall and transforms spectators into active participants, represents a continued trend toward immersive theatrical experiences that blur the line between performer and audience.

While the 2026 season is still unfolding, the early emphasis on smaller-scale, emotionally resonant productions suggests a Broadway landscape that values authenticity and direct human connection over spectacle. The success of shows like *Every Brilliant Thing* demonstrates audiences' appetite for theater that addresses mental health and personal struggle with both honesty and hope.

As spring approaches and more productions announce their openings, theatergoers seeking meaningful, conversation-starting experiences will find compelling options in this year's lineup. Check back regularly as additional shows debut throughout the season.
